beats.say: Solve seven to the power X minus one equals five to the power X minus three, to three significant figures.
asks: What does to the power X minus one mean?

beats.say: Seven and five cannot be made the same base, so we cannot just compare the powers.
asks: Why can't 7 and 5 be the same base?

beats.say: Here is the plan: the two sides are equal, so their logs are equal. Then bring the powers down.
asks: Why take log of both sides?

beats.say: Take log on both sides. Log seven to the power X minus one equals log five to the power X minus three.
asks: Why is it allowed to take log on both sides?

beats.say: Now bring the powers down, with the law Bring down power: log of A to the N is N times log A.
asks: Why does the power come down?

do.text: Bring down power: $\lg a^n = n\lg a$

beats.say: X minus one comes down in front of log seven.
asks: Why can the power come down?

beats.say: And X minus three comes down in front of log five.
Log seven and log five are just numbers, so solve it like normal algebra. Expand the brackets.
asks: Why are log 7 and log 5 just numbers?

beats.say: X terms to the left, number terms to the right.
asks: How do I move the terms across?
How do I factorise out x?

beats.say: Divide both sides by log seven minus log five, to get X on its own.
asks: Why divide by log 7 minus log 5?

beats.say: Press the calculator. X equals negative eight point five seven, correct to three significant figures.
asks: How do I key this into the calculator?
